core_obligations: Reduction (proof lines 1641-1644): the argument is said to mirror the module case, and it suffices to show that the displayed comparison map is surjective.

The preimages (proof lines 1644-1655): for a map into the colimit the author considers the subobjects of the source obtained as preimages of the stages, shows that the source is their union, and uses this to reduce surjectivity of the comparison map to a statement about those preimages.

Stabilisation (proof lines 1656-1667): a set of stages whose preimages cover one fixed preimage has cardinality at most the number of subobjects of the source, hence has an upper bound strictly below the given ordinal, so the fixed preimage equals the preimage of that bound and the map factors through it, which gives surjectivity and hence smallness.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the surjectivity of the comparison map.
Describe the source as the union of the preimages of the stages.
Use the cofinality hypothesis to find an upper bound stage and conclude the factorisation.
difficulty_reason: The proposition states that an object of a Grothendieck abelian category with at most kappa subobjects is alpha-small with respect to injections for every ordinal alpha of cofinality bigger than kappa (statement lines 1633-1639). The proof is a complete argument mirroring the module case: it suffices to show a displayed comparison map is surjective (proof lines 1641-1644); the source of a map into the colimit is written as the union of the preimages of the stages, which reduces the statement to those preimages (proof lines 1644-1655); and the set of stages whose preimages cover a fixed preimage is bounded in cardinality by the number of subobjects, so the cofinality hypothesis gives an upper bound stage and the factorisation follows (proof lines 1656-1667). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping of the preimages. The claim is H2.
